newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends down on commission/commercial sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends down on commission/commercial sales.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended lower Thursday, under pressure from both commission house and commercial selling, pit traders said.
Iowa Grain, ING and LIT were all prominent sellers of March and January in early trading, traders said.
"We just really didn't see much buying in here at all today (Thursday)," said one pit trader.
The January/March spread was the session's biggest feature. The spread traded at seven, eight, nine, 10, 11, and 12 cents per cwt, traders said.
Dean Witter was a buyer of the spread, traders said.
Shatkin, Arbor and Karlov were said to be buying January outright, traders said.
Some of the market's weakness was linked to modest farmer selling, traders with ties to the cash market said.
"They're using this market to price the new crop, so open interest is going to keep going up," the trader said.
Rice futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 500 contracts, below the 725 contracts traded Monday.
Rice closed 5 to 11 cents per cwt lower, with January down 11 at $10.92 per cwt.
